correctness.rationale: Order-continuity is first converted to Hausdorff continuity by compactness of the nested family. Centers are continuous because every subsequential center limit is a symmetry center of the Hausdorff limit, whose center is unique. A finite vector-rounding lemma approximates the total center displacement by twice a subset sum of arbitrarily small center increments with error at most d times the largest increment. Each selected increment is realized by two central reflections that are valid inside the corresponding nested sets. Closedness then gives the limiting recentered inclusion. The packaged exact checker validates the rounding mechanism and reflection algebra.

originality.rationale: Dawson's 2009 primary geometry paper explicitly conjectures that the Figure 1 failure of recentered containment cannot occur in a continuously indexed strongly nested family. The associated Open Problem Session asks the stronger strong-nesting question. A materially inspected 2010 follow-up develops monotone and Čebyšev arcs but does not contain the present recentering theorem. Searches under the exact conjecture, centered-translate formulations, and equivalent containment language found no covering result.
residual_risks: An unindexed later paper or note may have resolved Dawson's 2009 conjecture.
The accepted theorem does not resolve whether strong nesting itself survives recentering.

value.rationale: The theorem settles an explicit archive-era conjecture attached to a concrete recentering obstruction and substantially narrows the stronger published open problem: any remaining failure must be boundary contact, not loss of inclusion. The proof is dimension-uniform and works without convexity, so it gives a structural statement beyond the convex hyperspace framework that motivated the question.
